_comment_roles: owner and admin are COMPOSITE. require_role() in app/auth/middleware.py matches an exact string, and realm roles are otherwise flat -- without these composites an owner would hold only 'owner' and would be rejected by require_admin and require_viewer.

realm.name: admin
realm.description: Manage cameras, thresholds, and onboard viewers

_comment_smtp: Points at the mailpit container. Mail is captured in a web inbox at http://localhost:9025 and never leaves the host, so clicking an onboarding link in test cannot mail a real address.

clients._comment: Confidential: the secret stays server side (api/routes/auth.py does the token exchange), and a confidential client is what makes a service account possible at all.
clients._comment_dag: Direct access grants are OFF by default on new clients in recent Keycloak. The branded login form uses grant_type=password, so it must be on or every login returns 401.
clients._comment_sa: Service account = the client_credentials identity kc_admin.py uses to create users.
clients._comment_mapper: Publishes ww_tenant into the access token. Without it every onboarding request falls back to an extra Admin API lookup of the caller's own record (routes/users.py::_tenant_of_actor).

users._comment: Service account user. clientRoles here is what grants kc_admin.py the right to create users; without it every admin call returns 403.
Seed owner. Test-only credentials; prod seeds its owner through the Keycloak admin console.

_comment_tokens: Short access token so the frontend's refresh path is actually exercised in test rather than only in a long prod session.
